title: Great durability + vintage design = classic Corelle!
text:
Great durability + vintage design = classic Corelle!. Like many others, I grew up with several sets of Corelle dishes in my house, including pansies and the Christmas scene set, as well as coordinating bakers and accessories. So it was with no small sense of nostalgia (as well as a sense of pride that this line is still made in the USA) that I snapped these up (after moving into my own homes both stateside as well as overseas, the original set of Corelle is still in my childhood home). Oddly, these are not listed as Corelle plates, but most definitely are as they are marked on the back.

The weight and quality of these is on par with vintage Vitrelle glassware, and the decals are evenly placed (Corelle is dishwasher safe, but cannot be used in the oven or broiler). They are listed as chip and break resistant, and from long years of experience using Corelle (and dishwashing), it's quite likely the decals will eventually wear off, although the plates themselves are still serviceable 25+ years later. I also love that the manufacturing process uses 65% recycled glass. The packaging was very straightforward; all six plates were nestled into a slim cardboard box.

As a single household, this is the perfect-sized plate for me (I prefer serving meals on appetizer and salad plates as mealtimes largely involving mezze and grazing). They work well for serving appetizers, desserts, sandwiches, etc, and the retro print would be great fun for a potluck, mahjong gathering, or retro-themed party. These would also make a great gift for a new college student starting off on their own; I love the versatility, durability, and most of all, the fact that you can still find dishes made right here in the USA!
